You can send or open PDFs and images from another app in M24 PDF Scanner via Android Share or Open with. PDFs open the normal save-import dialog; shared or opened images open the Images to PDF flow. If App Lock is enabled, incoming files wait until the app is unlocked.
Tap the + button (bottom right) or choose Start Scanner from the menu.
The Google Document Scanner opens. Photograph one or more pages — edges and perspective are corrected automatically.
After scanning, a dialog appears. Enter a file name and tap Save. The PDF is stored locally on your device.
Tap an entry in the list to open the PDF in the in-app viewer. Use Open externally from the viewer if you want another app.
Tap the checkbox to select one or more entries. The title bar shows the count and lets you select all.
Tap + and choose Scan document to capture new pages with the system scanner. After saving, the PDF appears in your archive like any other document.
Tap + and choose Import PDF to open the system file picker. Select an existing PDF from your device; after saving, it is copied into the archive.
Use Share to send PDFs to other apps. Use Export to copy them to Downloads.
Opens the archive with your saved PDFs. From there you can open documents, select them, and start further actions.
Starts the document scanner so you can capture one or more pages and save them as a PDF.
Opens this help screen with the main functions and symbols used in the app.
Shows the app version, licenses, tech stack, and project credits.
Explains how the app works locally on your device and which data is not transmitted.
Shares the selected PDFs with other apps.
Exports the selected PDFs to your Downloads folder.
Select at least two PDFs and tap Merge to combine them into a new document.
Open the three-dot menu on a multi-page PDF and choose Split pages to create multiple PDFs at selected split points.
Open the three-dot menu and choose Reorder pages to rearrange pages via drag and drop or the up and down buttons.
Use Delete to move selected PDFs to trash. They can be restored for 30 days or deleted permanently from Trash.

Text Extraction (OCR) reads all pages. For a single document it opens OCR Review with per-page text, recognized language, and quality. For multiple documents it shows a combined panel where you can copy or share the result.
Make Searchable adds an invisible text layer to the PDF, stores the extracted OCR text locally for archive search.

OCR and Make Searchable use Automatic mode by default — works offline for Latin-script documents. Hindi, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean models are downloaded on first use via Google Play Services. Chinese, Japanese, and Korean are not supported for searchable PDF — use Extract Text to index them for search.
Use the hamburger menu (top left) to access the Archive, Trash, Settings, Help, Info, and Privacy screens.
The app does not require direct camera access — the ML Kit Document Scanner runs as a separate system process.
All PDFs are stored locally in the app directory and do not leave the device.
For multi-page documents, photograph multiple pages in sequence — the scanner automatically combines them into a single PDF.
OCR and PDF editing run locally on the device. Your documents are not uploaded by the app.

The app scans, imports, creates, appends, and views PDFs in-app, keeps deleted documents in trash for 30 days, performs on-device OCR, stores OCR text and quality metadata locally for archive search and OCR review, and offers page editing, annotations, signatures, metadata updates, grayscale conversion, protection, and secure redaction with optional OCR rebuild for redacted copies.

Android Print, Share, and Open with integration use system dialogs. Printing sends the selected PDF to Android Print; incoming PDFs and images shared to or opened in this app are copied into the app archive only after user confirmation.

No ads, no account, and no own backend. PDFs, thumbnails, generated copies, deleted items in trash, OCR text, and OCR quality metadata stay in app storage on your device until you export, share, or permanently delete them. Scanning, OCR, and downloadable models or fonts rely on Google Play Services; this app does not upload document content itself.
This app stores PDFs, thumbnails, image-to-PDF results, redacted copies, and optional searchable OCR text locally on your device.
Documents are not uploaded automatically. Sharing, printing, and exporting only happen when you explicitly trigger them. Secure redaction creates a new copy; the original remains until you delete it.

The scan and OCR functions use Google Play Services. Technical diagnostic data may be transmitted for error analysis. The automatic mode uses a bundled Latin text recognizer that works offline. Language models for Hindi, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean may be fetched via Play Services on first manual use — the content of your documents is not sent by this app.
The app itself collects no personal data, uses no own analytics, and requests no own network permission.

Open the three-dot menu and choose Rotate pages. Select the pages, choose 90°, 180°, or 270°, then apply the change.
Choose Delete pages to remove selected pages from a PDF. At least one page must remain in the document.
Choose Extract pages to save the selected pages as a new PDF.
Choose Duplicate pages to create a new PDF with copies of the selected pages.
Rotate, reorder, and delete pages can either replace the original PDF or save the result as a copy.
Choose Add page numbers to create a new PDF copy with centered page numbers on every page.
Choose Add text watermark to place custom text diagonally across every page in a new PDF copy.
Add page numbers to this PDF
The app creates a new PDF copy and places page numbers centered at the bottom of every page. Existing content and OCR text stay untouched.
Add a text watermark to this PDF
The watermark is applied diagonally across every page and saved as a new PDF copy. Existing content and OCR text stay untouched.
Create a smaller copy of this PDF
Compression creates a new PDF copy by recompressing the page images. Searchable PDFs are excluded in this version so their OCR text layer is not lost.
Searchable PDFs cannot be compressed in this version because the OCR text layer must stay intact
Unlock the PDF before compressing it
Protect this PDF with an opening password
The app creates a new password-protected PDF copy. The original file stays unchanged.
Remove the opening password from this PDF
Enter the current password to save an unprotected copy of this PDF.
Choose Compress PDF to create a smaller copy of a non-searchable PDF. The original file remains unchanged.
Export as JPG renders each page of the PDF as a JPEG image (150 DPI) and saves it to your Downloads folder. Single-page PDFs produce one file; multi-page PDFs produce one image per page.
Choose Set opening password to create a password-protected copy that requires the password when opening it.
Choose Remove opening password and enter the current password to save an unprotected copy.
Add a handwritten signature stamp to this PDF
Draw your signature, choose the target page, and save a new signed PDF copy. The signature is placed as a stamp at the bottom right of the selected page. Existing content and OCR text stay untouched.
Draw your signature in one or more strokes.
Unlock the PDF before editing it
Choose Sign PDF to draw a handwritten signature, choose the target page and stamp size, and save it as a new PDF copy.
Lift usage restrictions without entering a password

Some PDFs open without a password but have usage restrictions such as no printing or copying. This function lifts those restrictions and creates an unrestricted copy. The original file stays unchanged.\n\nNote: This does not remove an opening password. If the PDF requires a password to open, use \"Unlock PDF\" instead.
This PDF is protected with an opening password. Use \"Unlock PDF\" to enter the password.

Choose Remove restrictions to lift usage restrictions (e.g. no printing or copying) from PDFs that open without a password. This does not crack or remove an opening password — for that, use Unlock PDF.
Create a copy without the OCR text layer
Each page is re-rendered as an image and saved as a new PDF copy. The text layer is removed; the visual appearance stays unchanged. The original file is not modified.
This PDF does not have a text layer
Choose Remove text layer to create a copy of a searchable PDF without the invisible OCR text layer. The resulting copy is no longer searchable and no longer contributes OCR text to search.
Permanently remove content under black boxes
Drag rectangles over sensitive content. Affected pages are rebuilt as image-only pages with the black boxes burned in, then saved as a new redacted PDF copy. The original file stays unchanged.
Drag on the page to place a redaction box.
A new redacted copy is created. The original file remains unchanged and may still contain sensitive data.
Select at least one area to redact

Choose Secure Redaction to permanently remove content under black boxes. Drag rectangles over sensitive areas, then tap Save to review the warning, optional searchable PDF, and language before creating a new redacted copy. The original file stays unchanged, so only share the redacted copy.
Set usage rights via owner password

Creates a new PDF copy with usage restrictions controlled by an owner password. The document can still be opened without a password, but printing, copying, and editing can be individually restricted. The original file stays unchanged.
Choose Restrict usage rights to create a copy with an owner password that controls whether printing, copying, and editing are allowed. The document can still be opened without a password.
Choose a valid page order for the whole PDF
Mark text with a yellow highlighter

Drag over areas to highlight them in yellow. Switch to Pan/Zoom to zoom and move the page, then switch back to Draw to mark text. Navigate between pages to mark multiple pages. A new highlighted PDF copy will be created.
Drag over text to mark it.

Choose Highlight PDF to draw yellow highlights over the document. Searchable PDFs also offer Text snap, which aligns a stroke to detected text lines. Pan/Zoom lets you zoom and move the page; if no text line is matched, the app keeps the normal freehand highlight.
Tap the search field at the top to find documents by filename or stored OCR text. Search runs locally on your device and uses prefix matching, so "Rec" can find "Receipt".
When a document is made searchable, tags such as Invoice or Contract are assigned locally from OCR text and keywords. Tags appear as coloured labels below the file name.

Full-text search, searchable PDF generation, annotations with text snapping, secure redaction, grayscale conversion, and page/image rebuilds operate locally on your device. Newly created redacted copies strip OCR text, metadata, and interactive PDF elements from the saved output.

Choose Print PDF to send the document to a printer. The system print dialog opens where you can select the printer, page range, and number of copies.
Create a grayscale copy of this PDF
Each page is re-rendered without colour and saved as a new PDF copy with the suffix _SW. The original file stays unchanged. The text layer is not carried over — the result is an image-only PDF.
Choose Convert to Grayscale to save a black-and-white copy of the PDF. Each page is re-rendered without colour. The original stays unchanged.
Change title, author, creator, subject, and keywords. The PDF is updated in place. The creation date stays unchanged; the modification date is refreshed when you save.

Tap PDF Info to view and edit a document\'s embedded metadata — title, author, creator application, subject, keywords, and the creation and modification dates. Editable fields are written back into the same PDF file.
A file with that name already exists
Choose Rename PDF to give a document a new name. The file name must be unique in the archive. The .pdf extension is added automatically.
